rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all 10 peaks and identify the limiting separations. The moderate temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction, while the short gradient targets the 10-minute scoring window.
Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the crowded central peaks respond to reduced slope. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, leaving room to improve resolution without a time penalty.

The limiting pair improved substantially with a shallower gradient, so reduce the slope further. Raising the starting organic fraction trims the weak-solvent portion and should keep the last peak near or below 10 minutes while preserving early-peak separation.

Raise the starting organic fraction to bring the last peak below 10 minutes while slightly reducing gradient steepness to preserve the fully resolved central cluster. The early peaks have ample separation, making this a promising route to CRF 1.000.

Injection 4 already achieves the maximum CRF. Test a modest temperature increase to shorten retention while checking whether the limiting pair remains fully resolved; retain injection 4 as the proven optimum if selectivity worsens.

Return to the temperature and gradient slope that achieved CRF 1.000, but trim the endpoint to 0.65 and the gradient duration to 10 minutes. The last peak previously eluted near organic fraction 0.60, so all peaks should retain their successful separations and elute before the shortened gradient ends.

The maximum CRF is already secured, so explore a shorter fully resolved run at higher temperature. The central pair converged at 45 C; 55 C may separate it again after an elution-order reversal while reducing the last retention time.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope at 55 C to improve the new limiting pair, which is just below baseline resolution. The 8.54-minute last peak leaves time for this adjustment while targeting a fully resolved run shorter than injection 6.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 8's slope to test a shorter fully resolved separation. Monitor both the early peaks and the two close central pairs, since changing the starting composition can alter their resolution.

Restore the starting composition that preserved early and central separations, then use a slope between injections 7 and 8. This should shorten retention slightly relative to injection 8 while keeping the limiting resolution above 1.5.

With CRF 1.000 already secured, test a cooler selectivity regime with a steeper gradient for a potentially shorter fully resolved run. Cooling may separate the central cluster differently, while the steeper slope offsets the increased retention.

Return to the promising 55 C regime and lower the starting organic fraction to improve separation of the pair that deteriorated when phi0 increased. Test a steeper gradient to offset the added early retention and seek a shorter run while monitoring both close central pairs.

Increase the gradient slope modestly from injection 12 to shorten the last retention time while testing whether both close central pairs remain above R = 1.5. Keep the starting composition and temperature fixed to isolate the slope effect.

Lower the starting organic fraction to help separate the limiting central pair, while increasing the slope to seek an earlier last peak. This tests whether the improved selectivity from a weaker start can support a faster fully resolved separation.

With the maximum CRF secured, explore a faster high-temperature regime using a steeper gradient. The previously limiting pair may separate after an elution-order reversal, while the higher starting organic fraction and temperature should shorten retention.

Test a steeper gradient in the 60 C regime, where the close pair appears to have reversed order. Further steepening may increase its separation while shortening the run; monitor the neighboring pair for compression.

Trim injection 14's gradient endpoint while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and slope. This should reproduce the shortest fully resolved result so far, with the last peak at approximately 7.60 minutes and CRF 1.000.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a substantially faster gradient at an intermediate temperature for another favorable elution-order regime. Keep the weak starting composition to retain the early peaks, and check whether central-pair selectivity survives the increased compression.

Return to the shortest proven fully resolved regime and increase its slope slightly to test the speed limit. This isolates whether the two close central pairs retain R ≥ 1.5 as the last peak moves earlier than 7.60 minutes.

Test the intermediate cooler temperature with a faster gradient to look for a different fully resolved selectivity window. The 30 C and 40 C results bracket substantial changes in the central cluster, while the proven CRF 1.000 methods remain available.

Test whether the proven 40 C separation tolerates a higher starting organic fraction while preserving its successful gradient slope. This should shorten retention, but the early pair and central cluster must be checked for lost resolution.

Use a slope midway between injections 12 and 13 to target CRF 1.000 with slightly more resolution margin than the fastest proven method. The trimmed endpoint should still place the last peak within the gradient, with retention near 8 minutes.

Slightly flatten the gradient relative to injection 8 to seek a larger minimum-resolution margin while retaining CRF 1.000. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, and the two limiting central pairs are expected to have similar resolutions near 1.7.

Reduce the slope from injection 21 to recover its limiting central separation while retaining the shorter retention afforded by the higher starting organic fraction. This targets another fully resolved method with the last peak below 10 minutes.

Trim the gradient window around injection 23's elution range, using a nearly identical slope to retain its improved resolution margin. This targets CRF 1.000 with minimum resolution near 1.7 and the last peak around 9.3 minutes.
